mainTopic: How many כהנים serve with the תמיד, איל, and פר; the morning-only ניסוך המים; the afternoon logs; and why a זר may skin and cut a קרבן
overview: The amud opens with the closing line of the earlier discussion about the פייסות, the lotteries for Temple jobs. A new משנה then teaches that the תמיד is carried by 9 to 12 כהנים: 9 on a regular day, 10 on סוכות, 11 for the afternoon תמיד or on שבת, and 12 on a שבת during סוכות. The גמרא proves two ways that ניסוך המים is poured only with the morning תמיד: from the משנה's choice of example for 12, and from the story of the crowd pelting a כהן with their אתרוגים. A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי learns from ״וערכו עצים״ that the afternoon תמיד needs two logs carried by two כהנים. The גמרא defends that reading from the change in the Torah's wording. רבי חייא counts up to 16 כהנים in the פייס. Another ברייתא counts 17, and the גמרא explains that it follows רבי יהודה rather than רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. A second משנה gives the counts for an איל (11 כהנים) and a פר (24 כהנים), and limits these counts to קרבנות ציבור. The גמרא ends with חזקיה's proof that a זר may do the הפשט and ניתוח, because the Torah names כהנים only for placing the fire.

steps.title: Closing line: that view matches neither רבי אליעזר בן יעקב nor רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends by noting that a certain way of counting the lotteries fits neither רבי אליעזר בן יעקב nor רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That view is not like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the earlier discussion about the lotteries (פייסות). It finishes that topic so the next משנה can begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion tried to match a way of counting the lotteries to a known תנא. This line concludes that it fits neither: its list included a lottery for the coal pan (מחתה) and one for carrying the limbs up to the altar, which neither of these תנאים would accept together.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that view or that תנא)
Which is not in line with...

phrases.english: That one (that view)
is not in line with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
and not in line with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion carried over from the previous daf about counting the lotteries.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: That count of the lotteries cannot belong to either רבי אליעזר בן יעקב or רבי יהודה.

steps.title: משנה: the תמיד is brought by 9 to 12 כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that the תמיד is carried by 9, 10, 11, or 12 כהנים, never fewer and never more.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The daily offering is brought by nine, ten, eleven, or twelve כהנים. Not fewer and not more.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the overall rule: the number of כהנים who carry the תמיד ranges from 9 to 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the headline rule. The משנה gives only the numbers here and explains each number in the next lines. 'Not fewer and not more' sets 9 as the minimum and 12 as the maximum.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily communal offering, brought every morning and afternoon

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The daily offering is brought by nine,
by ten, by eleven, by twelve.
Not fewer and not more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the closing line before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תמיד is carried by between 9 and 12 כהנים.

steps.title: Explaining 9 and 10: a regular day and סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The תמיד itself needs 9 כהנים. On סוכות, one more כהן carries a jug of water for ניסוך המים, which makes 10.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? The offering itself is brought by nine. On סוכות, one more holds a jug of water. That makes ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts explaining its numbers. On a normal day there are 9 כהנים. On סוכות a tenth is added to carry the water for the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic 9 are the כהנים who carry the limbs, the flour offering, and the wine. On סוכות there is also a special water libation (ניסוך המים), so one extra כהן brings the water jug.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (the משנה is about to explain)

phrases.english: How so?
It itself is brought by nine.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּחָג, בְּיַד אֶחָד צְלוֹחִית שֶׁל מַיִם —
phrases.english: On the festival, in the hand of one is a jug of water —
so here there are ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the numbers listed in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Regular day: 9. On סוכות: 9 plus one for the water jug, which makes 10.

steps.title: Explaining 11: the afternoon תמיד with two logs
steps.stepSummary: For the afternoon תמיד, two more כהנים carry two logs of wood to the altar, which makes 11.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the afternoon there are eleven: the offering itself has nine, and two more carry two logs of wood in their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains one way to reach 11. At the afternoon תמיד, two extra כהנים bring two logs for the altar fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two logs are added to the altar fire with each תמיד. In the morning, carrying them is part of the job won in the first lottery, so nobody extra is needed. In the afternoon, two new כהנים carry them, which adds 2 to the basic 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The afternoon (time of the afternoon תמיד)
Logs / pieces of wood for the altar fire

steps.confusionAlert: Logs are placed in the morning too, so why do they add כהנים only in the afternoon? Because in the morning the logs are carried as part of the first lottery's job, and in the afternoon they need two separate carriers.

phrases.english: In the afternoon, by eleven:
it itself by nine,
and two have in their hands
two logs of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation and moves on to the number 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Afternoon תמיד: 9 plus 2 log carriers, which makes 11.

steps.title: Explaining 11 on שבת and 12 on שבת of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: On שבת, two כהנים carry the two dishes of frankincense from the לחם הפנים, which makes 11. On a שבת during סוכות, the water jug is added, which makes 12.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת there are eleven: the offering itself has nine, and two more carry the two dishes of frankincense of the showbread. On a שבת during סוכות, one more holds a jug of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second way to reach 11, which is שבת. It then shows the only way to reach 12: a שבת that falls during סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the two frankincense dishes (בזיכי לבונה) that sat with the לחם הפנים are burned, so two more carriers join the 9. When that שבת is also during סוכות, the water carrier is added on top, making 12. This is the maximum mentioned in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread on the שולחן, replaced every שבת
A שבת that falls during סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will build a proof from the fact that the משנה chose שבת of סוכות as its example of 12.

phrases.english: On Shabbat, by eleven:
it itself by nine,
and two have in their hands

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בְּזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
phrases.english: two dishes of frankincense of the showbread.
And on a Shabbat within the festival,
in the hand of one is a jug of water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the numbers with שבת (11) and שבת of סוכות (12).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת: 9 plus 2 frankincense carriers, which makes 11. שבת of סוכות: 11 plus the water carrier, which makes 12.
steps.whatToRemember: 9 is the base. Add 1 for water on סוכות, 2 for logs in the afternoon, and 2 for frankincense on שבת. The maximum of 12 comes on שבת during סוכות.

steps.title: Water is poured on סוכות only with the morning תמיד
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא (others say רמי בר חמא or רבי יוחנן) rules that ניסוך המים is done only with the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אבא said, and some say it was רמי בר חמא, and some say it was רבי יוחנן: On סוכות, water is poured only with the morning תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a new rule: the water libation on סוכות is done only in the morning, not with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never said directly when the water is poured. This אמורא draws a time limit for ניסוך המים: only the morning תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
And some say (it was a different speaker)
They pour (a libation on the altar)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Abba said,
and some say it was Rami bar Ḥama,
and some say it was Rabbi Yoḥanan:
They do not pour water on the festival
except with the morning daily offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new rule out of the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On סוכות, ניסוך המים is done only with the morning תמיד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the time of day for ניסוך המים.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a plain request for a source, not an attack. The answer will come from a close reading of the משנה.

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual basis for limiting ניסוך המים to the morning.

steps.title: The source: the משנה's case of שבת during סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The source is the משנה's line that on a שבת during סוכות, one כהן carries a jug of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that the משנה teaches: on a שבת during סוכות, one כהן holds a jug of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the exact line in the משנה that supports the rule. It quotes that line here and explains the logic in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on which example the משנה picked for 12 כהנים. It picked שבת of סוכות, not a regular weekday of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches

phrases.english: From the fact that it teaches:
And on a Shabbat within the festival,
in the hand of one is a jug of water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7 by quoting the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's case of שבת during סוכות is the source.

steps.title: Why the משנה's choice proves the rule
steps.stepSummary: If water were also poured in the afternoon, a weekday of סוכות would already have 12 כהנים: 9, plus 2 logs, plus 1 water. The משנה would not have needed שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you thought water is also poured with the afternoon תמיד, you could find twelve on a weekday too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה's example proves the rule. If water were poured in the afternoon, a regular weekday of סוכות would also reach 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Afternoon on a weekday of סוכות would be 9 plus 2 log carriers plus 1 water carrier, which is 12. Then the משנה would not have needed the special case of שבת. Since it chose שבת, water must not be poured in the afternoon.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה used שבת of סוכות as its example of 12. That shows ניסוך המים is not done with the afternoon תמיד, because otherwise a weekday afternoon of סוכות would already reach 12.

phrases.english: And if it should enter your mind
that they pour with the afternoon daily offering,
you would find it (twelve) on a weekday as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ בְּתָמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם מְנַסְּכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic behind the quote in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The rule in step 6 that ניסוך המים is only with the morning תמיד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה chose שבת of סוכות rather than a weekday afternoon of סוכות as its example of 12.

steps.title: רב אשי's second proof from the אתרוג story
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves that the water was poured only in the morning. In the משנה, the crowd pelted a wrong-doing כהן with their אתרוגים, and people hold אתרוגים in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this in a משנה. They would tell the כהן pouring the water, "Raise your hands." This is because once a כהן poured the water onto his feet, and all the people pelted him with their אתרוגים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second proof for the rule that ניסוך המים happens only with the morning תמיד. His proof is a story told in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crowd had אתרוגים in their hands when the water was poured. People carry their לולב and אתרוג in the morning, when they do the מצוה. So the pouring must have taken place in the morning, which supports the rule from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (introduces support from a משנה or ברייתא)
The כהן who pours the libation
Raise your hands (so everyone can see you pour correctly)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about why the כהן was punished. It is only about the fact that the people had אתרוגים in hand, which tells us the time of day was morning.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We too have also learned this:
And to the one who pours, they say to him:
"Raise your hands,"
phrases.notes: So that all can see the water going onto the altar

phrases.english: because one time someone poured
phrases.notes: A צדוקי כהן who rejected this מצוה

phrases.english: onto his feet,
and all the people pelted him with their etrogim.
phrases.notes: אתרוגים are in hand in the morning, so the pouring was in the morning

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent proof for the rule of step 6, after the proof in steps 8-9.
steps.raayaObject: That ניסוך המים is done only with the morning תמיד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about the כהן who was pelted with אתרוגים, which shows the event took place in the morning.

steps.title: Conclusion: the proof stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof. ניסוך המים is done only in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by accepting the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two proofs now support the rule that the water is poured only with the morning תמיד. The first is the count of כהנים, and the second is the אתרוג story. Nothing challenges them, so the rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: ניסוך המים is done only with the morning תמיד. Two things prove it: the count of 12 כהנים on שבת, and the אתרוגים in the crowd's hands.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ניסוך המים is done only with the morning תמיד.

steps.title: Source that the afternoon offering needs two logs and two priests
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי learns from ״וערכו עצים״ that the afternoon תמיד needs two logs carried by two כהנים. The morning already has its own verse, so this verse must refer to the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: How do we know that the afternoon תמיד needs two logs of wood, carried by two כהנים? The verse says, "And they shall arrange wood." This verse is not needed for the morning תמיד, because about the morning it is already written, "And the כהן shall burn wood on it every morning and arrange on it." So apply it to the afternoon תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a Torah source for the two logs at the afternoon תמיד. These are the two logs mentioned in the earlier count of כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse ״וערכו עצים״ uses plural forms: "they" points to two כהנים and "wood" points to two logs. The morning already has its own verse, ״ובער עליה הכהן עצים בבקר בבקר״. So this second verse is "extra," and we apply it to the afternoon.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for that topic, apply it elsewhere

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the "2 logs" in the count of כהנים used in steps 4 and 9.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
From where do we know regarding the afternoon daily offering
that it requires two logs of wood
carried by two priests?
As it says: "And they shall arrange wood."
phrases.notes: Plural: "they" means two priests, and "wood" means two logs

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
phrases.english: If it is not needed for the morning daily offering,
since it is written: "And the priest shall burn wood on it
every morning, and arrange on it,"

phrases.aramaic: תְּנֵיהוּ עִנְיָן לְתָמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם.
phrases.english: apply it to the afternoon daily offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a Torah source for the two logs that were part of the count of כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The afternoon תמיד requires two logs of wood brought by two כהנים, learned from the extra verse ״וערכו עצים״.

steps.title: Challenge: maybe both verses are about the morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that both verses may describe the morning. In that reading, the Torah is telling us to lay out wood in the morning twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that both this verse and that verse are about the morning תמיד. The Torah is saying: do it, and then do it again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reading. It argues that the second verse does not have to be moved to the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's proof only works if the second verse is "extra" for the morning. The challenge says it is not extra: both verses may describe two separate wood arrangements in the morning. If so, we have no source for the afternoon logs.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, both
Do it, and then do it again

phrases.english: But say that this one and that one
are both about the morning daily offering,
and the Merciful One is saying:
Do it, and then do it again!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the "אם אינו ענין" reasoning of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״וערכו עצים״ is not needed for the morning and must refer to the afternoon.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second verse could have its own purpose in the morning, namely a second arrangement of wood. Then it is not extra, and the afternoon derivation falls apart.

steps.title: Answer: the Torah would have repeated the same word
steps.stepSummary: If both verses were about the morning, the Torah should have said ״ובער״ twice. The change in wording shows that a different time is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have said "And he shall burn" and again "And he shall burn."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון בן יוחי by pointing to the different wording in the two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verses use different words, ״ובער״ and ״וערכו״. A simple repeat of the same act would most naturally use the same word twice. So the change suggests a different occasion, which is the afternoon.

phrases.english: If so,
the verse should say "And he shall burn," "And he shall burn."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual precision: the change in wording shows a different occasion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses describe two wood arrangements in the morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The different wording points to a separate time, the afternoon.

steps.title: Rejection: the change in wording may teach one priest, then two
steps.stepSummary: The change in wording may have a different purpose. It may teach that the first morning arrangement uses one כהן and the second uses two, so both could still be in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written "And he shall burn" twice, I would have thought: one כהן, yes; two, no. So it teaches us that we do it once with one and once with two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 14. It shows that the change in wording can be explained without moving the verse to the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״ובער״ is singular (one כהן) and ״וערכו״ is plural (two כהנים). The switch could simply teach that the second morning arrangement needs two כהנים. So the wording does not prove the verse is about the afternoon, and the challenge of step 13 is back.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not deny that the afternoon needs two logs. It only shows that the proof from the change in wording is not airtight. The next step answers this push-back.

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had written "And he shall burn" (both times),
I would have said:
one priest, yes; two, no.
So it teaches us
that we perform it with one, and perform it with two!
phrases.notes: Both could still be in the morning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 14, which brings back the challenge of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the change in wording. It does not reject the halacha of two logs in the afternoon.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The change from ״ובער״ to ״וערכו״ can be explained as one כהן versus two כהנים in the morning. It does not have to mean a different time of day.

steps.title: Same verb would have been used if only the number of priests changed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the change in wording only teaches one כהן versus two. If that were the point, the Torah would have kept the same verb and changed only singular to plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have said 'and he shall burn' and 'and they shall burn,' or 'and he shall lay out' and 'and they shall lay out.' Why does it say 'and he shall burn' and then 'and they shall lay out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against Step 15. That step said the change in wording only teaches one כהן versus two כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To teach one כהן versus two, the Torah only needed to change the verb from singular to plural, using the same verb both times. Instead it uses two completely different verbs, ״ובער״ and ״וערכו״. That extra change must teach something more, namely that the verses describe two different times of day.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a rebuttal showing what should have been written)
Let the verse say (the Torah should have written)
And he shall burn (kindle) the wood
And they shall lay out (arrange) the wood

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate changes happen between the verses. The verb changes from 'burn' to 'lay out,' and the number changes from 'he' to 'they.' The number change alone could teach one כהן versus two. The verb change is the extra detail that proves a different time is meant.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
'And he shall burn' and 'and they shall burn,'
phrases.notes: Same verb, changing only singular to plural.

phrases.english: or alternatively: 'and he shall lay out' and 'and they shall lay out,'
Why 'and he shall burn' and 'and they shall lay out'?
phrases.notes: Two different verbs signal two different times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the דחיה of Step 15 and restores the reading from Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual precision: the verb change is more than the singular/plural change requires
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The change in wording only teaches one כהן versus two, so both verses could be about the morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: A change in number alone would have kept the same verb. The different verbs show the verses refer to different times.

steps.title: Conclusion: the second verse refers to the afternoon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reading is correct. ״וערכו עצים״ refers to the afternoon תמיד, which needs two logs carried by two כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this as we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion. The original teaching about the afternoon logs is confirmed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two verses describe different times, ״וערכו עצים״ cannot be about the morning. It must be about the afternoon תמיד. The plural forms then teach two כהנים and two logs.
steps.whatToRemember: The afternoon תמיד requires two logs of wood carried by two כהנים. This comes from ״וערכו עצים״, which the different verbs prove refers to the afternoon.

phrases.english: Learn from this as we have said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the rebuttal in Step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״וערכו עצים״ refers to the afternoon תמיד: two כהנים bring two logs.

steps.title: How many priests are chosen in the second lottery
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that the second פייס chooses 13, 14, 15, or 16 כהנים, depending on the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: the lottery is sometimes for thirteen, sometimes fourteen, sometimes fifteen, sometimes sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. A ברייתא from רבי חייא counts how many כהנים the second פייס assigns to jobs for the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular day, 13 כהנים are chosen. On סוכות, a 14th is added to pour the ניסוך המים. On שבת, two more are added to burn the frankincense (the בזיכין), making 15. On a שבת that falls during סוכות, all three are added, making 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery used to assign Temple jobs
Bowls of frankincense burned on שבת (background, not in the text)

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to the earlier discussion. ניסוך המים is a morning job, which is why the water pourer can be counted in the morning פייס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
The lottery is sometimes for thirteen,
sometimes fourteen,
phrases.notes: On סוכות, add one more for the water pourer.

phrases.english: sometimes fifteen,
phrases.notes: On שבת, add two more for the frankincense.

phrases.english: sometimes sixteen.
phrases.notes: On a שבת during סוכות, add all three extras.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the number of כהנים in the פייס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second פייס chooses at most 16 כהנים: 13 base, plus 1 on סוכות, plus 2 on שבת.

steps.title: A teaching that says seventeen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא with another ברייתא that counts up to 17 כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: seventeen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. Another ברייתא gives a maximum of 17, not 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's highest count is 16. The other ברייתא counts one more job, so the two teachings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: seventeen!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חייא's maximum of 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's count of a maximum of 16 כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contradicting ברייתא gives a maximum of 17.

steps.title: The two teachings follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of 17 follows רבי יהודה, not רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. רבי חייא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so he counts only 16.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא is not like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, but like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The two ברייתות follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra 17th job is carrying the limbs from the ramp up to the מזבח. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that the same כהנים who brought the limbs to the ramp carry them up, so no new כהן is needed. The ברייתא of 17 adds a separate כהן for this job, which follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view רבי חייא follows (16)
The תנא whose view the ברייתא of 17 follows

steps.whatToRemember: 16 versus 17 is a dispute between תנאים. The 17th job is carrying the limbs up the ramp to the מזבח, and only רבי יהודה's view gives it to a separate כהן.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא names רבי אליעזר בן יעקב first only to say the ברייתא is NOT like him. רבי חייא's 16 is the one that follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: That one is not according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
but according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, אֶלָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree with no explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (16). The other ברייתא follows רבי יהודה (17).

steps.title: A ram is offered by eleven priests
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that an איל brought as a communal עולה is carried to the מזבח by eleven כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An איל is offered by eleven כהנים. The meat is carried by five. The innards, the flour, and the wine are carried by two כהנים each.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Earlier we learned how many כהנים carry the parts of a lamb, and now the משנה gives the count for a larger animal, the איל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ram is bigger than a lamb, so more כהנים are needed. The meat takes five. The innards, the flour of the מנחה, and the wine of the נסכים each need two כהנים, because a ram comes with larger amounts. That makes 5 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour, used for the מנחה
Wine, used for the נסכים (wine libation)

phrases.english: MISHNA: A ram is offered by eleven [priests]:
the meat by five,
the innards, and the fine flour, and the wine
by two [priests] each.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that continues the earlier topic of how many כהנים serve, now for a ram.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A communal ram is brought up by 11 כהנים: 5 for the meat and 2 each for the innards, flour, and wine.

steps.title: A bull is offered by twenty-four priests
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists how the parts of a פר are split among 24 כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bull is offered by twenty-four priests. For the head and the right leg: the head by one and the leg by two. For the tail and the left leg: the tail by two and the leg by two. For the breast and the neck: the breast by one and the neck by three. The two forelegs by two, the two flanks by two. The innards, the flour, and the wine by three each.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves up to the largest animal, the פר. It goes piece by piece and says how many כהנים carry each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a bull is so heavy, single pieces like a leg or the neck need two or three כהנים. The limbs add up to 15 (1+2+2+2+1+3+2+2). The innards, flour, and wine take three each, which adds 9, for a total of 24.

keyTerms.meaning: The sides or flanks (the rib sections)

steps.confusionAlert: Each pair (like 'the head and the leg') is a pair of pieces carried in the same round. The numbers after it tell you how many כהנים carry each piece, not the pair together.

phrases.english: A bull is offered by twenty-four [priests]:
the head and the [right] leg:
the head by one, and the leg by two.
the tail and the [left] leg:
the tail by two, and the leg by two.
the breast and the neck:
the breast by one, and the neck by three.
the two forelegs by two,
and the two flanks by two,
the innards, and the fine flour, and the wine
by three [priests] each.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list, moving from the ram to the bull.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A communal bull is brought up by 24 כהנים, with the heavier pieces split among two or three כהנים each.

steps.title: These counts apply only to communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the fixed counts to קרבנות ציבור. With a קרבן יחיד, one כהן may do it alone. The skinning and cutting are the same for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? With communal offerings. But with an individual's offering, if one priest wants to offer it, he may. The skinning and cutting of both kinds are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us when these fixed numbers of כהנים apply. It also adds one rule that is the same for both kinds of offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large public ceremony with many כהנים is only for קרבנות ציבור. For a private offering, one כהן may carry everything himself. The last line says the skinning and cutting of both kinds are 'equal', but it does not yet explain in what way. The גמרא will explain that next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When is this said?', a phrase that limits a rule to certain cases
Communal offerings, brought for the whole nation
A private offering, brought by one person
Cutting the animal into its limbs

phrases.english: In what [case] are these things said?
With communal offerings.
But with an individual's offering,
if [one priest] wishes to offer [it alone], he may offer.
Their skinning and their cutting,
of these and of those, are equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the counts in steps 21 and 22 to קרבנות ציבור and adds a rule shared by both kinds of offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fixed numbers apply only to קרבנות ציבור. A קרבן יחיד may be offered by one כהן. הפשט and ניתוח are the same for both.

steps.title: Equal means both may be done by a non-priest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה's word 'equal': for both kinds of offerings, הפשט and ניתוח may be done by a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: their skinning and cutting are equal in that they may be done by a זר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that explains the unclear word 'equal' at the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the two are 'equal' without saying how. The ברייתא tells us: in both a קרבן יחיד and a קרבן ציבור, a non-כהן may skin and cut the animal. These jobs do not need a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
'It was taught', which introduces a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: 'Equal' here does not mean the same number of כהנים. It means that for both kinds of offerings, even a non-כהן may do these jobs.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
Their skinning and cutting are equal in [being valid by] a non-priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last word of the משנה in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For every offering, הפשט and ניתוח are valid when done by a זר.

steps.title: חזקיה asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה asks where we learn that a זר may do the skinning and cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: From where do we know that skinning and cutting are equal in being valid by a זר?
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה asks for the Torah source of the rule we just learned. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most work with קרבנות must be done by a כהן, so letting a זר do part of it needs a source. חזקיה looks for a פסוק to support the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא in ארץ ישראל
'From where?', a request for a source

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:
From where [do we know] regarding skinning and cutting
that it is equally [valid] by a non-priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source of the ברייתא in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows הפשט and ניתוח do not need a כהן.

steps.title: Only the fire needs a priest
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers from the פסוק: it names בני אהרן for placing the fire, but not for the skinning and cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'The sons of אהרן the כהן shall place fire on the altar.' Placing fire needs כהונה. Skinning and cutting do not need כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives his source. The Torah mentions כהנים only when it reaches the job of placing the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק just before this one says 'he shall skin the עולה and cut it into pieces' and does not mention כהנים. Then the next פסוק says 'the sons of אהרן the כהן shall place fire.' Since the Torah brings in כהנים only at the fire, we learn that the earlier jobs, הפשט and ניתוח, may be done by anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Priesthood, meaning the job must be done by a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: A זר may skin and cut any קרבן. The Torah names כהנים only for the later step of placing the fire.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method of learning: when the Torah names כהנים for one job but not for the job right before it, we learn that the earlier job does not need a כהן.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'The sons of Aaron the priest shall place
fire on the altar.'
Placing fire requires priesthood;
skinning and cutting do not require priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְנָתְנוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן אֵשׁ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חזקיה's question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah names בני אהרן only for placing the fire, not for the skinning and cutting in the פסוק before it. So הפשט and ניתוח do not need כהונה.
